=== page 4 ===
The sol–gel process was employed because of the intimate mixing of the constituent elements that can be achieved through this process, thereby enabling good compositional control and purity.^[35–39]
=== page 12 ===
Experimental Section
Sol–Gel Method for the Synthesis of NFA Materials: The cathode materials were synthesized using the sol–gel process. Appropriate molar quantities of nickel acetate (Sigma-Aldrich), iron acetate (Sigma-Aldrich), aluminum acetate (Sigma-Aldrich), and lithium acetate (Sigma-Aldrich) were dissolved in a solution of citric acid (Sigma-Aldrich) and deionized water with the ratio of citric acid to transition metals maintained at 1:1. The solution was continuously stirred and evaporated at 60 °C until a solid gel was formed. The resulting product was dried at 100 °C overnight followed by drying in air at 400 °C for 4 h. The final cathode material was obtained by grinding and calcining the preheated powders in an oxygen atmosphere at 750 °C for 20 h.

So, the temperatures the sol-gel precursor passed through are:
1. 60 °C
2. 100 °C
3. 400 °C
4. 750 °C

The final calcination lasted for 20 hours.
